deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics: no derivations, formulas or computations. It is a handwritten bibliography headed 'Vollständige Liste von Eulers Werken' (complete list of Euler's works), with the subheading 'Einzelne Werke' (separately published works). It lists Euler's books in chronological order with place, year and format (4 = quarto, 8 = octavo):

- Dissertatio physica de sono (Basel 1727)
- Mechanica sive motus scientia analytice exposita (St Petersburg 1736, 2 vols)
- Einleitung zur Rechen-Kunst, here called 'Einleitung zur Arithmetick' (Petersburg 1738, 2 parts)
- Tentamen novae theoriae musicae (1739)
- Methodus inveniendi lineas curvas maximi minimive proprietate gaudentes (Lausanne 1744)
- Theoria motuum planetarum et cometarum (Berlin 1744)
- Beantwortung verschiedener Fragen über die Beschaffenheit, Bewegung und Würkung der Cometen, with its Fortsetzung (Berlin 1744)
- Neue Grundsätze der Artillerie, translated from Benjamin Robins with notes (Berlin 1745)
- Opuscula varii argumenti, here 'Varia Opuscula' (Berlin 1746, 1750, 1751; 3 vols containing 6, 4 and 3 treatises)
- Novae et correctae tabulae ad loca lunae computanda (Berlin 1746)
- Tabulae astronomicae solis et lunae (same place and year)
- Gedanken von den Elementen der Körper (Berlin 1746)
- Rettung der [Göttlichen] Offenbarung gegen die Einwürfe der Freygeister (Berlin 1747)
- Introductio in analysin infinitorum (Lausanne 1748, 2 vols)
- Scientia navalis (St Petersburg 1749, 2 vols)

The list continues on the next page through the Opuscula analytica (1783–85).

Context: the previous page is the printed table of contents of an elementary arithmetic and algebra textbook. That is plausibly Christian Leiste's textbook, given the bundle name 'HB.Leiste'. This leaf is therefore a handwritten addition bound into or interleaved with that book.

The hand is plausibly the young Gauss's, but this is not certain from the page alone. The list resembles the Euler bibliographies that circulated after Euler's death in 1783, for example those derived from N. Fuss's Éloge.
errors: The 'Einleitung zur Rechen-Kunst' appeared in two volumes, 1738 and 1740. Giving only '1738' for both parts is a simplification.
The exact Latin title is 'Novae et correctae tabulae ad loca lunae computanda'; the list has 'Noua & correcta tabulae'. This is a minor slip in the original or a sloppy copy.
The exact title is 'Introductio in analysin infinitorum'; the list has 'ad analysin'. This is a common variant.
The exact title is 'Opuscula varii argumenti'; the list has 'Varia Opuscula'. This is a paraphrase.
The 'Tabulae astronomicae solis et lunae' were issued within Opuscula vol. 1 (1746) rather than as a fully separate book. Listing them separately is defensible but imprecise.
Otherwise the dates and places agree with the standard Euler bibliography (Eneström).

results.what: Chronological bibliography of Euler's separately published books, 1727–1749 (continued on the next page)
results.usually_credited_to: N. Fuss (1783 Éloge list); G. Eneström (1910–13)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copied bibliographic list of Euler's works with no mathematical content. That a young reader of Euler, Gauss or a fellow student of Leiste's textbook, compiled such a list is entirely unremarkable.
transcription_corrections: The machine transcription of this page is essentially correct. The title 'Vollständige Liste von Eulers Werken' and the subheading 'Einzelne Werke' are confirmed by the image.
In the previous-page margin fragments, 'Singulae[?]' is actually 'Einzelne [Werke]' and 'Crantzuorly[?]' is actually 'Beantwortung'. These are the cut-off edges of this same page.
'Hrn. B. Robins' refers to Benjamin Robins.
After 'Cometen Berlin 1744' there is an ink blot over the format digit, which is presumably '8'.
